A Generative Adversarial Network (GAN) is a type of neural network architecture used to generate new data samples.
The core of a GAN consists of two neural networks: a generator and a discriminator. The discriminator network takes data samples and outputs a probability of them being real or fake.
The generator network takes random noise as input and produces a new data sample.
An adversarial relationship exists between the two networks. The generator's goal is to produce outputs that fool the discriminator. The discriminator's goal is to correctly classify the real data as real or fake and the generated data as fake. This creates an adversarial game. The two networks improve iteratively until the discriminator can no longer tell the difference between the real and generated data. At that point, the generator has learned to mimic the distribution of the real data and the discriminator can no longer differentiate. The output of the GAN is a new data sample
